gta-6-platforms.title: GTA 6 Platforms: PS5 and Xbox Series X|S Confirmed — What About PC?
gta-6-platforms.excerpt: GTA 6 launches November 19, 2026 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S — the only confirmed platforms. PC, PS4, Switch 2 and Game Pass are not announced. Here is exactly what is confirmed, and what is not.
gta-6-platforms.content:
The short answer: GTA 6 launches on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026 — those are the only platforms Rockstar has confirmed (✅ Rockstar-confirmed). There is no announced PC version, no PS4 or Xbox One version, and no Switch 2 or Game Pass announcement. Everything below separates what is confirmed from what is still open, so you can plan your hardware with your eyes open.

Confirmed: PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026

Rockstar announced GTA 6 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and both official trailers close on those same two platforms. The release date — November 19, 2026 — applies to both (✅ Rockstar-confirmed). If you own a PS5 (disc or digital) or an Xbox Series X or Series S, you are covered on day one; no other hardware has been promised anything.

Two details are worth knowing. First, Rockstar has not announced separate editions or platform-exclusive content, so any retailer listing a "PS5 exclusive edition" is guessing (❓ unconfirmed). Second, performance targets — resolution and frame rate on each console — have not been announced either. Anyone quoting an official "4K 60fps" figure today is inventing it.

Is GTA 6 coming to PC?

Not announced (❓). Rockstar's official platform list contains consoles only, and the company has said nothing about a PC version, a PC release window, or PC pre-orders. Our dedicated guide on the GTA 6 PC release date tracks every official signal.

What history suggests — and this is pattern analysis, not a confirmation: GTA V launched on PS3 and Xbox 360 in September 2013, reached PS4 and Xbox One in November 2014, and arrived on PC in April 2015, roughly 19 months after the first console launch. Red Dead Redemption 2 followed the same shape: consoles in October 2018, PC in November 2019, about 12 months later. Rockstar's modern pattern is console first, PC later and enhanced. A PC version of GTA 6 is widely expected on that basis, but until Rockstar announces it, the only honest label is ❓ unconfirmed.

What about PS4 and Xbox One?

Not announced — and realistically, do not plan around it. Rockstar's announcement names PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only, and nothing in either trailer suggests a last-generation version exists. The world shown in the trailers — dense crowds, large draw distances, seamless interiors — is built around current-generation CPUs and fast SSD storage that the PS4 and Xbox One simply do not have. Our honest read: a PS4 or Xbox One version is very unlikely (❓ expectation, not an official statement — Rockstar has not commented on last-gen either way). If you are still on last-gen hardware, the upgrade window is the year between now and November 2026.

Xbox Series S: the version to watch

The Series S is a confirmed launch platform — it sits inside "Xbox Series X|S" (✅ Rockstar-confirmed). It is also the least powerful confirmed machine, with a weaker GPU and less memory headroom than the Series X and PS5. That makes it the technical floor Rockstar is designing around, which is genuinely good news for everyone: a game that runs well on Series S scales up, not down. What we do not know is how it will run — resolution and frame-rate targets for Series S are unannounced (❓). If Series S performance is your deciding factor, wait for post-announcement hands-on coverage rather than pre-launch promises.

PS5 Pro, Switch 2 and handhelds

PS5 Pro: the console runs PS5 software, so GTA 6 will play on it — but a dedicated PS5 Pro enhanced patch has not been announced (❓). Nintendo Switch 2: no announcement (❓), and given the hardware gap, treat any "Switch 2 port confirmed" post as fiction until Rockstar says otherwise. PC handhelds (Steam Deck, ROG Ally): these depend entirely on the unannounced PC version, so there is nothing confirmed to plan around today.

Game Pass and PS Plus

GTA 6 is not announced for Xbox Game Pass or PlayStation Plus at launch (❓ not announced). Rockstar's parent company has publicly resisted day-one subscription launches for its biggest titles, and GTA V's appearances in subscription libraries have always come years after release. Plan on buying the game if you want to play in November 2026.

Which platform should you choose?

If you already own a PS5 or Xbox Series console, the choice is simple: play where your friends and your library are — the game is the same. If you are buying hardware for GTA 6, the PS5 and Series X are the full-fat options, the Series S is the budget route with unannounced performance targets, and the PS5 Pro is the premium pick if you value headroom for a possible enhanced patch. If you are a PC-only player, the honest options are patience — Rockstar's history says a PC version is a matter of when, not if — or a console for launch year. We track every platform development on gta6mapx, with each claim labeled by evidence.

GTA 6 platforms — FAQ

Q: Is GTA 6 coming to PS4?
A: Not announced. Rockstar lists PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only, and a last-gen version is considered very unlikely (❓).

Q: Will GTA 6 be on PC at launch?
A: No PC version has been announced (❓). Rockstar's history with GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 points to a later, enhanced PC release — but that is a pattern, not a promise.

Q: Is GTA 6 on Xbox Series S?
A: Yes — Series S is included in the confirmed "Xbox Series X|S" launch platforms (✅ Rockstar-confirmed). Performance targets are unannounced.

Q: Is GTA 6 coming to Game Pass?
A: Not announced (❓). Do not count on a day-one subscription release.

Q: Which console runs GTA 6 best?
A: Unknown until Rockstar publishes performance details. On paper the PS5 Pro has the strongest hardware; official modes and frame rates are unannounced (❓).

gta-6-system-requirements.title: GTA 6 System Requirements: No Official PC Specs Yet — What to Expect
gta-6-system-requirements.excerpt: Rockstar has published no official GTA 6 system requirements, because no PC version is announced. This guide gives you the console hardware baseline, clearly-labeled PC estimates, and how to prepare.
gta-6-system-requirements.content:
The honest answer first: Rockstar has published no official GTA 6 system requirements — because no PC version of GTA 6 has been announced. The game launches on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026 (✅ Rockstar-confirmed). Any website listing exact "official" PC specs today is guessing. What we can do — and what this guide does — is show you the console hardware GTA 6 is actually built for, give you clearly-labeled PC estimates based on it, and tell you how to prepare without wasting money.

Why there are no official GTA 6 system requirements

System requirements are published for a specific version of a game. Rockstar has announced GTA 6 for consoles only, so there is no PC build to spec against — no minimum GPU, no RAM figure, no storage number. That will change if and when a PC version is announced: Rockstar published full PC requirements for GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 ahead of those launches, and the same will happen here. Until then, every requirement in this guide that is not a console fact is marked as an estimate (❓), because that is what it is.

The real baseline: the hardware GTA 6 is built for

The most reliable guide to GTA 6's demands is the hardware it must run on (public manufacturer specifications):

PlayStation 5: 8-core AMD Zen 2 CPU, RDNA 2 GPU (10.28 TFLOPS), 16GB GDDR6 memory, custom NVMe SSD (~5.5 GB/s raw read).
Xbox Series X: 8-core Zen 2 CPU, RDNA 2 GPU (12 TFLOPS), 16GB GDDR6, NVMe SSD (~2.4 GB/s raw).
Xbox Series S: 8-core Zen 2 CPU, RDNA 2 GPU (4 TFLOPS), 10GB GDDR6, NVMe SSD — the weakest confirmed target, and therefore the floor the game is designed around.

Two conclusions follow. The CPU bar is a modern 8-core design, not an extreme one. And every confirmed platform has a fast SSD — asset streaming at SSD speed is a design assumption, not an optional extra.

Estimated PC requirements (our estimate — not official)

Translating the console baseline into PC parts, our estimates are:

Estimated minimum (1080p, low/medium settings): 6–8 core CPU in the Ryzen 5 3600 / Core i5-10400 class or better; GPU in the RTX 3060 / RX 6600 class (roughly PS5-equivalent raster power); 16GB RAM; NVMe SSD storage.
Estimated recommended (1440p–4K, high settings): Ryzen 7 5800X / Core i7-12700 class CPU; RTX 4070 / RX 7800 XT class GPU or better; 16–32GB RAM; fast Gen 4 NVMe SSD.

Read those as planning ranges, not promises (❓ estimates). Where they could move: if the PC version ships with heavier ray tracing than the console build, GPU demands rise; if it is a conservative port of the Series S build, they fall. We will replace these estimates with Rockstar's official table the day it exists.

The one requirement that is close to certain: an SSD

Every platform GTA 6 is confirmed for stores the game on a fast NVMe SSD, and both trailers show the kind of dense, fast-moving world — highway chases through detailed streets, crowded beaches, seamless city-to-wetland transitions — that is built to stream from fast storage. GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 on PC already treat an SSD as the practical baseline for acceptable loading and texture streaming. If your PC still boots from a hard drive, an NVMe SSD is the single upgrade most likely to matter for GTA 6, and it is the cheapest one to make now.

Storage size: not announced

Rockstar has not published GTA 6's install size (❓ not announced) — be skeptical of exact figures circulating on social media. For scale only: Red Dead Redemption 2's PC install is roughly 119GB and GTA V's current PC install is around 110GB. A game of GTA 6's scope landing somewhere in that territory would surprise nobody, but the real number arrives with the official requirements or the console store listings.

How to prepare your PC now

Three sensible steps, in order. First, the SSD: if you lack an NVMe drive, that is upgrade number one — it helps every game, not just this one. Second, RAM: 16GB is the realistic floor for a modern open-world release; moving from 8GB to 16GB is inexpensive and overdue for most older builds. Third, wait on the GPU: graphics cards are the expensive part, and buying against estimates a year-plus before a PC announcement is how money gets wasted — GPU value improves every generation, and official requirements will tell you exactly where the bar sits. Keep following the PC release date guide and this page; both are updated the moment Rockstar publishes anything official.

GTA 6 system requirements — FAQ

Q: What are the official GTA 6 PC system requirements?
A: There are none yet. No PC version has been announced, so Rockstar has published no requirements (✅ that absence is the current fact).

Q: Can my current PC run GTA 6?
A: Nobody can answer officially yet. If your PC is at or above the estimate ranges above — RTX 3060-class GPU, 16GB RAM, NVMe SSD — you are plausibly in range for a future PC version (❓ estimate).

Q: When will official requirements be announced?
A: With a PC version announcement, whenever that comes. Rockstar's pattern with GTA V and RDR2 was full specs ahead of the PC launch.

Q: Will GTA 6 run on Steam Deck?
A: Unknown — it depends on the unannounced PC version's demands and optimization. The Series S being a confirmed target is mildly encouraging, nothing more (❓).

Q: How much storage will GTA 6 need?
A: Not announced (❓). Comparable Rockstar PC installs (RDR2 ~119GB, GTA V ~110GB) suggest planning for 100GB+ of free SSD space as a cautious guess.

How the Six Regions Add Up to One Map

This section is analysis, working from the six confirmed region names and what those names describe. Vice City is the compact one: a dense city packs content into a small footprint, so it adds detail rather than distance.

The distance comes from everything around it. Leonida Keys reads as an island chain, so ❓ water would separate each piece and ❓ boat travel would likely be the quickest way to cover it. Grassrivers suggests a wide river system, which is linear travel rather than circular.

Port Gellhorn reads as a compact coastal town. Mount Kalaga National Park is a protected area, and a park of that kind takes more ground than a town of equal importance. Ambrosia is the one we can say least about, since its name carries no obvious geography.

Put those six together and the state covers a city, an island chain, a river region, a port and a national park, which points to a state-sized layout rather than a single-city sandbox. ❓ Estimate on the second measure: crossing Leonida from one edge to the other takes hours of driving, not the short hop that links neighbourhoods in older entries. Island chains and river systems make that worse, since you cannot drive straight across them.

❓ Estimate on the third: we expect the gap between GTA 6 and earlier open-world releases to be significant rather than marginal, in the direction Rockstar's worlds have grown since 2013. We are not attaching a multiplier. A figure like "three times" would be invented precision.

Why the Real Footprint Stays Unknown Until Release

Rockstar's history explains part of the gap. GTA V launched on console in September 2013 and reached PC in April 2015, roughly 19 months later. Red Dead Redemption 2 went from console in October 2018 to PC in November 2019, about 12 months. ❓ Pattern analysis: that is the usual stretch before a Rockstar world gets properly documented, since PC players map it in detail first.

Until then, the real limits sit inside the build. Whatever in-game map, draw distance and water boundaries the game ships with can only be measured with the game running, and any fast travel grid it ships with would only make the picture clearer.
